findings.title: Hot lead-config writes projects.json only; the launch manifest + launchd plist env are asserted launch inputs, not just evidence — next Lead launch can hard-fail
findings.detail: §3.1 confines the registry write to projects.json ('Bridge 按自身部署 state root 选文件'), and §3.5 / operator.md classify '启动 manifest/env' as startup *evidence* ('不是当前实际模型'). That is wrong about this repo. packages/teamlead/scripts/lib/canonical-lead-identity.sh:34-43 defines canonical_lead_identity_assert_existing() as `[ -n "$actual" ] && [ "$actual" != "$expected" ] -> canonical_lead_identity_fail identity_env_conflict; return 1`, and lines 138-140 apply it to FLYWHEEL_LEAD_MODEL, FLYWHEEL_LEAD_EFFORT and FLYWHEEL_LEAD_MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOW against the value resolved from projects.json. Every Codex Lead launcher sources it under `set -euo pipefail` (packages/teamlead/scripts/codex-lead.sh:17,117; run-codex-lead-mufasa-tui-fullaccess.sh:30,54 — the CLAUDE.md-mandated production TUI form), so a mismatch aborts the launcher rather than warning. The plist env is not hand-written: scripts/flywheel-daemon.sh:356-359 and scripts/flywheel-fleet.sh:997-1001 project manifest `.model`/`.effort` into EnvironmentVariables.FLYWHEEL_LEAD_MODEL/FLYWHEEL_LEAD_EFFORT on every plist (re)generation, deleting the key only when the manifest field is empty. The plan's named target already carries such a field: ~/.flywheel/manifests/raya-raya.json has "model": "gpt-6-astra" today (its plist happens to be env-free right now, which is why this is latent rather than already broken). Failure scenario: operator runs `lead-config set --project raya --lead raya --model <new>`; projects.json now says <new> while the manifest still says gpt-6-astra; any later plist regeneration (daemon install/reinstall, fleet apply, restart-services) bakes FLYWHEEL_LEAD_MODEL=gpt-6-astra into the plist; the next physical Lead launch resolves canonical=<new>, hits identity_env_conflict, returns 1, and set -e kills the launcher -> the Lead crash-loops and is down, caused by a change the design markets as 'no restart needed'. 13 of 17 live com.flywheel.lead.*.plist files already carry FLYWHEEL_LEAD_MODEL, so the carrier is in routine use. The plan needs an explicit coherence contract: either update ~/.flywheel/manifests/<leadKey>.json (and the plist EnvironmentVariables projection) inside the same cfglock transaction as projects.json, or refuse the hot write when a manifest/plist carrier for the target is non-empty — and say which, with a test. Today §3.5 only promises 'Fleet展示 desired/applied/observed' and 'consumer sweep覆盖 fleet-data、fleet-capabilities、management-topology-source、management-existing-writers及命令渲染', none of which touches the manifest or the plist generator.

findings.title: §2.3 step 3's 'active run' guard has no defined status set; 'active' is a literal value distinct from 'held', and held legacy runs resume into the live_template branch
findings.detail: §2.3 step 3 specifies the only protection for legacy unpinned runs as '查目标所有 active run：若 snapshot 无法验证，或任一可执行节点缺 dispatchPinned:true，409 active_run_not_pinned'. It never defines what 'active' means, and in this schema that word is a *specific literal*: workflow_run.status DEFAULT 'active' (StateStore.ts:26778), with 'held' as a separate non-terminal value. Held runs are not finished — StateStore.ts:37355, 49274 and 50436 all flip `status = 'active' WHERE run_id = ? AND status = 'held'`, and 49380/49432 advance current_node_id while held; the codebase's own live-set predicate elsewhere is `status IN ('active','held')` (StateStore.ts:13498). Failure scenario: a pre-dispatchPinned run for tpl_simple_code is parked in status='held' awaiting a founder gate. The publish guard is implemented literally as `SELECT ... FROM workflow_run WHERE template_id = ? AND status = 'active'` — the held run is invisible, the guard passes, and the new revision commits. The run later resumes to active and launches its next node; because its snapshot node lacks dispatchPinned, workflow-dispatch-resolution.ts:120-158 takes the `source: "live_template"` branch, reads template.current_published_revision, and dispatches the *newly published* vendor/model/effort. That is precisely the harm the guard exists to prevent, it silently violates §1's founder-facing promise '发布前 run 的后续 implement 保持旧版', and A4's assertion '不改legacy快照' would still pass because the snapshot bytes genuinely did not change — only the resolution did. The plan must name the exact non-terminal status set the guard queries (and pin it with a test that parks a legacy unpinned run in 'held' and asserts active_run_not_pinned).

findings.title: §3.3 says 'reuse existing HMAC' but canonicalRequest() has a per-method allowlist with a default branch that would leave the new config fields unsigned — and still authenticate
findings.detail: CodexLeadInboxSocket.ts:595-627 canonicalRequest() is a switch over method with an explicit field list per branch; anything not matched falls through to the submitBatch shape `JSON.stringify({version, method, leadId, ownerEpoch, batch})`. signRequest()/authenticateRequest() (lines 631-647) HMAC exactly that string. So if `applyRuntimeConfig` is added without its own branch, JSON.stringify drops the undefined `batch` and the signature covers only {version, method, leadId, ownerEpoch} — model, effort, operationId, configDigest, configGeneration and modelRegistryRevision would all be unsigned, yet authenticateRequest() returns true, so the omission is completely silent. Failure scenario: one legitimate applyRuntimeConfig frame is observed on the socket; it is replayed with model/effort swapped to any other value and passes HMAC verification, changing the Lead's model for all subsequent turns. §3.3 lists what the *body contains* and what the server *rebinds* (projectName/leadKey/identityDigest/socketOwnerId/ownerEpoch) but never states the canonicalization invariant. Add it as an explicit requirement plus a negative test (tampered model/effort must fail auth), since the surrounding trust boundary is already documented as same-UID and therefore cannot absorb an unsigned field.

findings.title: §3.1 mandates 'the same projects.json.cfglock' but the repo resolves that path through three mutually incompatible mechanisms
findings.detail: §3.1 says '复用 scripts/flywheel-config-lock.sh 的 projects.json.cfglock' and §3.2 relies on '持同一 cfglock' for mutual exclusion. There is no single resolution rule to reuse: scripts/flywheel-fleet.sh:1421 and scripts/flywheel-fleet-batch.sh:300 use `${FLEET_CONFIG_LOCK_FILE:-${PROJECTS_JSON}.cfglock}`; scripts/migrate-summary-registry.sh:18 uses a *different* variable, `${FLYWHEEL_CONFIG_LOCK_FILE:-${PROJECTS_PATH}.cfglock}`; and packages/teamlead/src/bin/backend-migration-config-lock.ts:26 hardcodes `join(input.home, ".flywheel/projects.json.cfglock")`, honouring neither override. Failure scenario: the isolated QA slot §3.1 requires ('隔离副本必须自己的 root') sets FLEET_CONFIG_LOCK_FILE to redirect the fleet engine's lock; the new lead-config writer reads FLYWHEEL_CONFIG_LOCK_FILE (or derives from its own state root) and takes a different lock file; both writers then believe they hold the projects.json write lock, run their read-check-write critical sections concurrently, and the loser's atomic rename silently discards the winner's change — while §3.2's recovery logic classifies the result as an untraceable third-party edit. Pin the exact env-var precedence and derivation the new writer uses, and assert in T3 that it resolves to the same path the fleet engine would.

findings.title: T3 invents a third registry-write discipline (scripts/lead-config-write.mjs) alongside two existing hardened Node-side primitives
findings.detail: §3.1/T3 introduce 'scripts/lead-config-write.mjs' as a new 'small restart-free registry write helper'. Two review-hardened primitives already do exactly this job. (1) packages/teamlead/src/bin/backend-migration-config-lock.ts exposes withMigrationConfigLock(): it spawns the python flock helper with a latch child, performs the handshake, and exposes an assertHeld() the caller must re-check after every await — the precise contract §3.2 describes in prose. (2) packages/flywheel-comm/src/commands/lead-registry.ts:604-609 (also :928, :1097) implements the established shell-holds-flock / Node-writes convention: the writer refuses unless FLYWHEEL_SUMMARY_CONFIG_LOCK_HELD=1, re-opens the file no-follow immediately before mutation, re-compares sha256 against the read image, and commits via writeAtomic()+fsyncDirectory() (lines 121-133). Failure scenario: the new .mjs reimplements the crash seams from scratch and gets one wrong — e.g. omits the fsyncDirectory after rename, or does not re-open no-follow before the CAS — so a seam that the existing helpers already survive reappears, and T3's 'rename每个crash seam' test matrix has to re-derive coverage that already exists. The plan should either reuse these (and say which) or state concretely why neither fits.

findings.title: '--from seed' cannot honour §2.3's single frozen modelSnapshot: the seed compile path resolves model aliases against the ambient snapshot, and workflow-menu.ts is in no task's file list
findings.detail: §2.1 requires the seed to be compiled per-request while '记录 build SHA 与 model-registry revision', and §2.3 requires '固定一次 modelSnapshot, 严格验证全部新 manifest'. The seed compile path cannot obey that today: resolveAlias() (workflow-menu.ts:233-251) takes `modelConfig: ModelConfigSnapshot = getModelConfigSnapshot()`, and the three call sites on the compile path — workflow-menu.ts:279, :280 and :306, reached from compileWorkflowMenuSeed -> menuFromGraph -> loadWorkflowMenuSeeds (:382) — all call it with **no** snapshot argument, so each falls back to the ambient global at call time. menuFromGraph (:167-169) has no snapshot parameter to thread one through. Failure scenario: stage compiles the seed and freezes digest D under registry generation G; the model registry rolls to G+1 between stage and apply; apply recompiles the seed against the ambient G+1 snapshot, producing different resolved vendor/model bytes than D, and the plan's only stated defence ('核 model-registry revision 仍等于stage') is a revision equality check that the seed compile never actually consulted. Neither T1 nor T2 lists packages/teamlead/src/workflow-menu.ts among their 'precise files', so there is no hook to thread the frozen snapshot through.

findings.title: §3.4 models drift only for the registry file; the founder's TUI is a concurrent writer to the very session settings this design claims to own
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md makes every production Codex Lead a windowed `codex resume --remote` TUI the founder can drive, and that TUI writes thread settings itself — codex-rs/tui/src/app_server_session.rs:140 (THREAD_SETTINGS_UPDATE_METHOD) driven from codex-rs/tui/src/app/thread_settings.rs:29-59 builds ThreadSettingsUpdateParams with model/effort. §3.4's drift detection is '每次 sidecar router turn 前和每次 raw turn/started观察后重新校验 current registry digest' plus an `external_registry_change` actor for direct *file* edits; nothing reconciles the runtime's actual session settings against the registry. Failure scenario: an operator runs `lead-config set --effort high`, the coordinator records applied/observed; ten minutes later the founder types /model in the Lead's TUI pane and lowers effort; the registry digest is unchanged so every re-validation passes, and `lead-config status` keeps reporting applied/observed=high while every subsequent turn actually runs at the founder's value — the founder-facing 'which round used which value' ledger §1 promises becomes silently wrong. §3.3 already specifies a `readRuntimeConfig` method on the socket; the plan should state where it is used to close this loop (and whether a founder-originated thread/settings/updated can be distinguished from the coordinator's own, since the design matches applied-ness purely on exact model+effort values).

findings.title: Every thread/resume re-sends the launch-frozen env model/effort; §3.5 asks for replay-on-reconnect but never says to stop sending the stale pair
findings.detail: §3.4 states '不能用被冻结的启动值覆盖刚更新的会话' and §3.5 states '重连先重放当前已提交配置，匹配后恢复 router admission', but the mechanism that reintroduces the frozen values is untouched. codex-lead-tui-runtime.ts:905 builds threadParams once from the launch config and reuses it at :1046 (`p.resumeThread(saved, threadParams)`) and :1057; codex-lead-runtime.ts:1661/1707/1722/1725 do the same. buildThreadParams (codex-lead-runtime.ts:1087-1129) emits `params.model` and `params.config.model_reasoning_effort` from FLYWHEEL_LEAD_MODEL/FLYWHEEL_LEAD_EFFORT, which were parsed once at process start (codex-lead-runtime.ts:717-741). Failure scenario: config is hot-applied to effort=high; the app-server child exits and the supervisor respawns it; the runtime resumes the saved thread with config.model_reasoning_effort=<launch value>; the founder takes a manual TUI turn before Bridge's reconcile replays the committed config — that turn runs at the old effort while the ledger still reads applied. Worth noting the two channels are not even the same protocol field: start/resume sets effort as a raw TOML override (model_reasoning_effort) while the hot path sets the typed ThreadSettingsOverrides.effort; the plan should assert their equivalence and order the resume/replay explicitly rather than leaving it to '必须在上线前QA证明其重连配置顺序'.

findings.title: §2.5's promised '只报告内容不同' is unreachable: preflight's seed_content_hash shortcut precedes the founder-owned branch, and manual publishes never move that hash
findings.detail: §2.5 says startup must not overwrite a manual publication and should '只报告内容不同'. The non-overwrite half holds, but the report half cannot fire in a common case. createAndPublishWorkflowTemplateRevision (StateStore.ts:29368-29476) sets seed_owner='founder' but never writes seed_content_hash, so after a `--from file` publish the row still carries the deployed seed's hash. On restart, preflightWorkflowCatalogMigration checks `existing?.seed_content_hash === seed.contentHash` FIRST (StateStore.ts:29795-29805) and returns status 'unchanged' with expectedRevision = current, so control never reaches the founder_owned branch at :29806-29879 that builds the seed_update audit with currentSeedContentHash/targetSeedContentHash. Failure scenario: the published manifest differs materially from the deployed seed, yet the restart emits no seed_update audit and no '内容不同' warning at all — the operator gets silence where the plan promises a report. Emitting it requires comparing the *published revision's* manifest digest against the seed digest, and neither preflightWorkflowCatalogMigration nor workflow-catalog-migration.ts appears in any task's file list.

findings.title: §2.1 cites buildWorkflowMenuSeeds(); the symbol does not exist
findings.detail: §2.1 says 'seed 从部署中的 `buildWorkflowMenuSeeds()` 按请求构造'. Grepping the repo for that identifier returns exactly one hit — this line of plan.md. The real exported symbol is loadWorkflowMenuSeeds() (packages/teamlead/src/workflow-menu.ts:382), which is what bridge/plugin.ts:5436 calls at boot; research.md cites it correctly at 'workflow-menu.ts:382', so the drift was introduced in the plan. Failure scenario: an implementer follows the plan's named symbol, finds nothing, and either re-derives the seed compile inline (defeating §2.1's 'seed 从部署中的...不是从任意开发 checkout 读取') or stalls. One-word fix, but this is the single symbol the whole `--from seed` source contract hangs on.

findings.title: §2.4 names a retention classification ('never-delete') that is not in the registry's closed vocabulary
findings.detail: §2.4 says the new workflow_template_publish_receipt should '注册 retention 分类…可在任务范围内先归 never-delete', and T5 asks to '确认所有新表retention分类'. After FLY-2413 (commit 5ad7b9853) the registry is a set of per-table JSON fragments under scripts/lib/fly-2006-retention-tables/{teamlead,comm}/<table>.json with a closed vocabulary of exactly four values in use: protectedCurrentOrReference (169), protectedAuthority (40), deleteTarget (21), retiredOptional (3) — 'never-delete' is not among them. The sibling tables are already classified (workflow_template_audit.json / workflow_template_publication.json / workflow_template_revision.json are all protectedCurrentOrReference). Failure scenario: the implementer writes classification "never-delete" into the fragment; createSchemaAssertions' registryNames() flattens the registry object's values, the unknown key is not a recognised classification bucket, and the schema assertion path (assertNoUnclassifiedSchema -> schema_unclassified, or a silently empty bucket) fails or mis-reports at CI time rather than at review time. Name the intended existing value, and note that registration is a new JSON fragment, not a code edit — the lead_config_operation and lead_config_audit tables in §3.2 need fragments too.
